Also δn := maxT diamround ϕn(T) → 0, where T ranges over flags. Every complete primal or dual incidence star consequently has diameter at most 2δn. (ii) Finitely many conditionally uniform rerootings may be retained using the same map and the same ϕn. (2.4) For µh-almost every z, the fiber η−1 r ({z}) consists of one time among all of [0, 1]. For two conditionally independent uniform rerootings, their limiting root positions, jointly with µh, have the law of two independent samples from µh conditional on µh. They are distinct almost surely. (iii) For each finite contour reference sphere, the projection Pn places every point of each flag at a vanishing maximum ρref-distance from ηref(t), over all tour representatives t of its quadrangle corners and all occurrences of its incident primal or dual vertices. The homeomorphisms satisfy sup x∈Xn ρref Ψn(x), Pn(x)  −→ 0. On further subsequences, ϕn ◦Ψ−1 n : Sref → S2 converges uniformly in the target round metric on S2 to the conformal or anticonformal three-point comparison map. The sign is retained in the coupling. For each member K ⋐ U of a fixed finite family, protection chooses a finite union I of tour intervals with (ηref )−1 (K) ⊂ I ⋐ (ηref )−1 (U). 8 Eventually I contains every tour representative of each flag whose contour projection meets K and of the full incidence stars of its three vertices. Intervals are interpreted on the time circle for a sphere and are bounded in the bilateral case. In a protected bilateral window the finite sewing leaves these stars unchanged, including cyclic order and original primal incidences. The homeomorphism of this protected bilateral sewing has projection error tending to zero over the tests, and its full inverse image of K lies in the unchanged part. The eventual index may depend on the tests and the sample. (iv) For either rerooting with root p∗, adjoin two independent auxiliary pairs of µh-samples conditional on the surface, independently of retained exploration and chart observa- tions given that surface and its contour. Use the separate three-marked representations (Q1, Q2, p∗) = (0, 1, ∞) and (Q3, Q4, p∗) = (0, 1, ∞). In either representation the chart interiors are relatively compact disks U ⋐ C \ {0, 1}, with the required strict buffers, on which the law of the actual-height sphere real-field restriction to U is abso- lutely continuous with respect to the local reference field law fixed for that comparison in Section 3. The two chart families cover S2 \{p∗}; the families for two distinct roots have a finite subcover of S2. Each comparison is used only in its own three-marked marginal, without conditioning on the other auxiliary pair. The geometric conclusions persist on any further jointly tight extraction that retains additional random observations of the maps and contours.
